rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 1 line 23 'The reasons for personal-first land in Phase 3' — a forward pointer, but it names the destination heading explicitly (Phase 3, an actual `##` that exists at chunk 5) instead of leaning on an unresolved pronoun. All in-file backward references resolve against an earlier chunk of the same file: chunk 5 line 58 'wrote it in Phase 1' → chunk 1; chunk 5 line 58 'Phase 2's invoke-and-critique' → chunks 3+4 (the un-headed 'Sharpen the skill' section is Phase 2's own continuation, same pairing pattern as chunk 1/2's 'Phase 1' / 'Answer from...' split); chunk 4 line 52 'Module 3 installs' and chunk 7 line 71 'Module 4 reads this skill' are arc-earned module-name vocabulary (carve-out). Chunk 7 line 74 'came over at the fork' resolves via the session-artifacts carve-out — same sentence already names 'the side-quest worktree' as the live session state in front of the student. Re-checked chunk 6 line 67 'The module's close sharpens it from what the invocation showed' this pass: not a coined proper term needing prior naming (unlike 'the loop'/'the verifier'), reads as plain English for 'the end of the module', and resolves against a real beat — `grep -n 'author-test-strategy-skill' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/pre-cohort-todos.md` this session surfaces the actual M3 closer prompt (`ae101-m3-sharpen-skill`) that does this sharpening — so it isn't even a dangling forward pointer, just under-specific narration about a beat that exists (rule 3 territory, also clear). Also re-checked chunk 0 line 13 post-fix: 'Authoring conversations spiral here' — 'Authoring' is grounded by chunk 0 line 7 ('author a test-strategy skill for your codebase through conversation'), same chunk as the note itself; 'here' is deictic to the current exercise (Window/Time chrome, lines 3/5), not a broken pointer.

No 'the opening lecture said' style backward callback into another file's content anywhere in the body. Closest candidate: chunk 7 line 71 'Module 4 reads this skill' — names the destination module by number, doesn't quote or locate content inside it by position, and functions as a closer pointing forward (permitted per §2's own text on closers). Chunk 6 line 67 'The module's close' is the same shape — names the beat by its functional role, not by page position.

rules_evaluated.evidence: RESOLVED since the prior instance's REVISE. `grep -c 'longest beat' curriculum/exercises/author-test-strategy-skill.md` this session → 0; `grep -ci 'Authoring conversations spiral here' curriculum/exercises/author-test-strategy-skill.md` this session → 1. Keep it tight: one author pass, one self-critique, one invocation, ship.' — the offending word 'beat' (a named specimen in this rule's own dialect list) is gone; the superlative claim it sat inside ('the longest beat in Module 3') is also gone, not renamed, per the commit message (`ac93ec5c`): the claim was false (three M3 exercises are stamped 20 minutes each — a three-way tie, not a superlative), so dropping rather than relabeling was the correct move, not a word-swap that would have left a false claim standing under different vocabulary. `grep -inE '\bsurface\b|\bfiring\b|\bcompendium\b|\bforcing function\b|\bbeat\b|\bmood\b|\bConnections\b' <(sed -n '1,75p' curriculum/exercises/author-test-strategy-skill.md)` this session → 0 hits: no other repo-internal dialect term anywhere in body. The fixed sentence still carries its operational content (spiral risk + the fix: one pass, one critique, one invocation, ship) — the beat that mattered (the timebox warning) is intact, only the false/jargon-laden decoration is gone.
